items.detail: The **Nasdaq** fell 1.07% to 25,164.32 Monday, pushing the Nasdaq-100 into a correction, while the S&P 500 lost 0.51% for a third straight decline.
items.why: New chip selling on doubts about AI profits outweighed an early rally sparked by oil's plunge.

items.detail: US crude dropped **7.36%** to $96.46 Monday, helping lift the Dow 0.41% even as tech stocks fell.
items.why: Iran's foreign minister said a deal with the US is possible, raising hopes that supply risks will ease.

items.detail: Apple beat forecasts as iPhone revenue rose **17%**, but the stock slipped after hours and S&P futures were flat on midterm election day.
items.why: Rising memory-chip costs and a weaker margin outlook took the shine off the beat, ahead of Friday's payrolls.

items.detail: South Korea's **Kospi** fell as much as 3.77% to 5,638 Tuesday, wiping out Monday's 2.2% rebound, and Taiwan's index dropped about 3%.
items.why: A 3.37% overnight slide in US chip stocks on AI profit doubts hit Samsung and SK Hynix.

items.detail: The **Nifty** jumped 1.68% to 23,440.80 Monday for a third straight gain, led by a 12% surge in Reliance, then opened higher again Tuesday.
items.why: Cheaper oil helps India as a big importer, and strong earnings brought foreign buyers back.

items.detail: The US **Russell 2000** slipped 0.2% to 2,805.88 Monday, now well below Thursday's 2,859 high and no longer rising as tech falls.
items.why: An early lift from cheaper oil faded as chip selling dragged the whole market lower into the close.

items.detail: **Bitcoin** is stuck near $77,000, down about 2% over the past day, and has not recovered from last week's Binance-hack selloff.
items.why: US spot bitcoin ETFs lost $399 million Monday, led by BlackRock's fund, a second big day of outflows.

items.detail: **Ether** is holding near **$2,260**, only slightly above last week's post-hack low, after losing 16% in October.
items.why: US spot ether ETFs saw record outflows of $1.61 billion in October, so big buyers are still pulling back.

items.detail: **Solana** is trading near **$94**, below its 200-day average for the first time since August, down about 22% in a month.
items.why: Breaking the $100 floor set off more selling, and dip buyers have not stepped in.

items.detail: **Gold** broke below $4,000, hit a yearly low near $3,870 overnight, and then recovered to about $3,950.
items.why: Oil's plunge eased inflation fears and supported the bounce, but gold stays below all of its major moving averages.

crossCuttingTheme: Doubts about AI profits are still driving selling in chip stocks from the Nasdaq to Seoul and Taipei. Meanwhile, oil's 7% drop on hopes for US-Iran talks is lifting India and helped gold rebound from its yearly low.
